#1489. GdS: Amorim ‘changes the pieces’ – his plan to rotate vs. Ferencvaros in must-win game

AC Milan don’t have much time to enjoy their derby win over Inter, as a key European game awaits on Thursday night.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by writing that this week marks the beginning of a genuine push toward success in the Europa League. The momentum gained from the derby victory must be harnessed and used properly.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For a Milan side capable of dismantling Chivu’s team with three goals in 45 minutes, the Ferencváros game should pose no real concern. It must, however, be approached with focus and a significant yet carefully considered rotation of the squad.

The situation mirrors the league campaign in one key respect: the table. By winning on Saturday, Milan got back into the hunt for the Scudetto, so a similar result is needed in Europe. The Rossoneri currently sit on three points, while the Hungarians have a perfect record of nine.

Even with a win, Milan won’t catch their opponents, but they will improve their position in the table which is a necessity, especially with only four games left after this.

Ferencvaros’ position in the standings is the result of a long, arduous journey. They began their Europa League campaign in the first qualifying round, eliminating Serbia’s Vojvodina.

In the second round, they knocked out the Dutch side Twente. They then triumphed over Poland’s Górnik Zabrze in the third round, before defeating Trabzonspor in the play-offs.

All that hard work has paid off in the league phase, where they have secured three wins out of three – against Celtic, Plzeň and Torreense – making them one of only five teams with a perfect record. The others are Benfica, Leverkusen, Bournemouth and Olympiacos.

Two of these four have already faced the Rossoneri, which speaks to the challenging nature of Milan’s schedule. Against the Portuguese side, Amorim faltered in his debut, fielding a side packed with reserves in a high-profile match.

Against Bournemouth, the result was compromised by two penalties and Mike Maignan’s red card. In between, there was a resounding victory in Salzburg, spearheaded by Alphadjo Cissé. This explains why they currently sit on just three points, a situation that now demands a turnaround.

The upcoming schedule is relatively more manageable, featuring an away trip to Athens, a home match against Sunderland, a visit to Sofia to face Levski, and a game against Ararat Armenia in Milan.

Securing a spot in the round of 16 is a task that needs to be completed, and preferably soon. Sitting on three points in 24th place, Milan’s current standing in the Europa League does not reflect the goal the club have set for themselves: to go all the way in the competition.

Cisse will return to the starting line-up for the competition in which he is the team’s top scorer: three goals, all netted on the same night in Austria. The squad will once again be adjusted to accommodate the turnover and rotations necessary for managing resources.

This time, the team are better prepared to absorb these changes after welcoming back some players before the derby. Consequently, there will be further rotation on Thursday night, with the aim of keeping everyone fresh.

A change is unavoidable in goal, where the suspension for the captain Maignan will see Lorenzo Torriani make his first start. In defence, Sankhoun Diawara could play centrally, while Pervis Estupinan or Davide Bartesaghi (or both, with the latter pushed further forward) could feature on the left.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will take on a Modrić-like role, while the versatile Filippo Terracciano could slot in as a mezzala (or even at right-back, covering for Mario Gila). There is also a chance of seeing the very young Christian Comotto in action.

In attack, Omari Hutchinson is a certain starter:he looked lively during his time on the pitch against Bologna and performed even better against Udinese, a match in which he scored his first goal for Milan. Cisse could lead the line, but Francesco Camarda and Goncalo Ramos remain candidates too.

Gerry Cardinale has declared that AC Milan will be active in the winter mercato, but who is on the potential shopping list?

Calciomercato.com write that Milan are constantly evolving, with owner Gerry Cardinale fully immersed in the club’s dynamics, aiming to create a winning team. The foundations have been laid with the signings of Mario Gila, Diego Moreira and Goncalo Ramos from the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then came the renewals of two key players, Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic. Official announcements regarding the contract extensions of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse, two of the players who have had a devastating impact this start to the season.

However, Cardinale spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport and revealed a desire to do more: “We need to continue improving the squad because I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted in the summer. It will probably take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.

“We’re only a quarter of the way there, and the priority is building a team that can deal with injuries. That’s why we’ll continue to be aggressive in the January transfer market. I won’t waste money, but when I set my mind on signing a player, I do everything I can to achieve it.”

There’s no doubt about one thing: Milan will sign a defender in January. Maybe two. The hottest name – Ruben Amorim’s favourite – is Goncalo Inacio from Sporting CP, with whom discussions began last summer.

Also on the list is Kim Min-Jae at Bayern Munich, with direct contact having been established in recent days. Looking to the future, Borussia Dortmund’s Luca Reggiani and Manchester United’s Leny Yoro are being eyed.

A potential right-back signing is also being considered: Argentine international Agustin Giay is among those being monitored . The 22-year-old from Palmeiras is worth around €13m.

In midfield, Pierre-Emile Højbjerg remains a real possibility for January if Milan decides to sign a central midfielder in the January transfer window. In that case, Christian Comotto would be loaned out: Parma, Monza, and half of Serie B are following him.

Sassuolo’s Darryl Bakola is highly sought after, while Bournemouth’s Alex Scott is the dream for next season. Two players Milan are following are the Swede Yasin Ayari and the Paraguayan Diego Gomez of Brighton. Cagliari’s Alessandro Romano is also highly sought after.

The idea is to make a five-star signing for the attack, and Cardinale’s obsession is Real Madrid’s Endrick. Nicolo Tresoldi is liked, but the problem remains Club Brugge who are tough negotiators. For the future, the focus is on Cagliari’s Paul Mendy and Monza’s Gustavo Varela.

Brighton & Hove Albion will continue their Conference League league stage campaign with a clash against La Liga outfit Getafe on Thursday.

Getafe opened their 2026-27 Conference League league stage campaign with a 1-1 draw against Univ. Craiova on October 15 before losing 5-2 to Lugano last time out, with one point from two matches leaving them in 30th spot in the overall table.

#1485. Boga’s limited minutes put focus on Zhegrova before Lazio

Luciano Spalletti outlined different considerations for Jérémie Boga and Edon Zhegrova before Juventus faced Lazio: Boga was fit for around half an hour, while Zhegrova’s performances had earned him a case for more playing time. His remarks, reported by Pazzi di Fanta and echoed in Juventus’ official press-conference account, point to contrasting immediate options rather than a settled hierarchy.

The distinction is grounded in what Spalletti said about their readiness and impact, not in an announced tactical role for either player. Boga remained available, but with his minutes limited; Zhegrova had impressed the coach with qualities and unpredictable play. Juventus’ official account also said the winger could start against Lazio.

For Boga, the clearest point was physical: Spalletti said he had about 30 minutes in his legs. That makes him an option for a defined contribution, rather than a player the coach said was ready to last a full match. It does not mean Boga was unavailable or ruled out of the selection.

Zhegrova’s case was different. Spalletti praised the qualities he had shown and said his performances warranted more playing time. The official Juventus account added that his unpredictable play could surprise opponents, while also reporting that he could start against Lazio.

That contrast suggests Zhegrova offered a possible route to changing the match through his attacking unpredictability, whereas Boga’s immediate involvement was constrained by fitness. It is an interpretation of Spalletti’s comments, not confirmation that the coach assigned them fixed or mutually exclusive positions. The pair’s different recent contributions have also featured in Juventus coverage of Zhegrova’s attacking impact.

Spalletti’s comments on team balance add an important qualification. The official account said the coach was weighing how to fit several attacking players into the side, taking both the opponent and the team’s overall balance into consideration. Praise for Zhegrova did not, by itself, guarantee a starting place.

The coach also rejected a rigid division between starters and substitutes, saying Juventus needed to widen the group of players considered starters. He was still assessing his selection and how the game might develop, with the possibility that starting certain attackers together would leave fewer options to influence the match later.

That broader approach prevents a simple reading in which Boga becomes a permanent bench option and Zhegrova takes over a defined role. Spalletti’s remarks were about the choices available for this fixture: Boga could contribute for roughly half an hour, while Zhegrova’s performances had strengthened his claim to more minutes. Neither statement settles their status over the season.

There is also a difference between being praised and being selected. Spalletti’s assessment gave Zhegrova positive momentum, and Juventus’ account explicitly left open a start against Lazio, but the coach said the final decision still depended on balance and the opposition. Boga, meanwhile, remained available within the fitness limit Spalletti had described.

The immediate comparison is therefore one of management: Boga’s involvement had a stated physical ceiling, while Zhegrova’s was supported by the coach’s view of his performances and unpredictability. That points to different ways they might help Juventus, without establishing a permanent tactical distinction. Boga’s recent place in the side has also been discussed alongside his selection in an attacking role.

Spalletti’s comments leave the practical question to the team selection and the match itself. Juventus’ official account said Zhegrova could start; Boga was available for around 30 minutes. Those were the clearest parameters ahead of Lazio, with no fixed pecking order announced.

Federica Mancuso has followed Juventus through every high and low she can remember, growing up in Turin where the club was never just a team but a way of life. Her writing focuses on what actually happens on the pitch, breaking down formations, pressing structures, and the tactical decisions that often go unnoticed in match coverage. She believes understanding how Juventus play is just as important as knowing the scoreline.

#1484. Trabzonspor vs Freiburg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 03 Nov 2026 19:56

Unbeaten in the 2026-27 UEFA Conference League so far, Trabzonspor will look to maintain their perfect record when they welcome Freiburg to Papara Park on Thursday.

The Turkish side have collected six points from their opening two league-phase fixtures and arrive on the back of seven consecutive victories across all competitions, while the visitors have recovered from a difficult spell with successive domestic wins ahead of their trip to Turkey.

Trabzonspor have emerged as one of the Conference League's early pace-setters under Thomas Reis, with their impressive domestic form translating into European success.

The Black Sea Storm began their continental campaign with an entertaining 4-2 victory away to KuPS, before returning to Papara Park to beat Hearts 2-0 on matchday two.

Those results came either side of an equally encouraging 2-0 home victory over Besiktas in the Super Lig, while subsequent league wins against Caykur Rizespor (4-3) and Gaziantep (2-0) have extended their winning sequence to seven matches.

Trabzonspor have six consecutive victories at Papara Park, and they have a significant European milestone within reach if they make it seven in a row, as a third successive victory in major continental competition would represent their best such run since November 2013.

Winning their opening three matches of a European campaign would also be only the second time they have achieved that feat, and they will hope to do just that in what will be their first ever meeting against the visitors.

However, Freiburg should provide a considerably different examination from Trabzonspor's previous European opponents.

The German side reached last season's Europa League final before losing to Aston Villa in Istanbul, and their experience at a higher level of continental competition means they should not be underestimated despite their inconsistent beginning to this campaign.

Julian Schuster's side opened their Conference League campaign with a 3-2 victory over Jablonec, but their trip to Monaco proved considerably more difficult, as they suffered a 3-0 defeat, which they followed with a 3-1 loss to Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga.

However, their domestic performances improved, with a 3-2 victory over Wolfsburg in the DFB-Pokal followed by a 2-1 away success against Augsburg.

Nevertheless, their European away record remains a concern, having lost four of their previous five matches on the road in continental competition.

Trabzonspor have several selection concerns heading into Thursday's encounter, with Aral Simsir, Franculino, Arseniy Batagov, Ruslan Malinovskyi and Okay Yokuslu among those expected to miss out.

Cihan Canak and goalkeeper Onuralp Cevikkan are also doubts, while Sidny Lopes Cabral is suspended following his dismissal against Hearts.

Paul Onuachu is another player whose involvement requires monitoring, although the Nigerian forward returned to the starting lineup against Gaziantep after missing two league matches through injury.

Freiburg are expected to be without Philipp Treu, who is struggling with an ankle injury, while Florent Muslija remains sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury.

Schuster should nevertheless have considerable experience available in central defence through Matthias Ginter and Philipp Lienhart, while Maximilian Eggestein and Yannik Engelhardt are options in midfield.

Vincenzo Grifo, Yuito Suzuki and Jan-Niklas Beste could provide the creativity behind Igor Matanovic, who has scored in each of Freiburg's last two matches.

Onana; Pina, Nwaiwu, Savic, Eskihellac; Fabinho, Kabasakal; Salah, Muci, Saviolo; Onuachu

Backhaus; Kubler, Ginter, Lienhart, Makengo; Eggestein, Engelhardt; Beste, Suzuki, Scherhant; Matanovic

Trabzonspor's outstanding home form, attacking consistency and confidence from seven consecutive victories make them difficult to oppose, particularly against a Freiburg side that have struggled to reproduce their domestic performances in European away fixtures.

#1483. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a big moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

#1481. Spalletti identifies Juventus changes after 3-0 Lazio loss

Luciano Spalletti said Juventus were inferior to Lazio after their 3-0 home defeat on Sunday, 18 October, admitting the performance had surprised him. The assessment, reported by Football Italia, came just days after the Bianconeri had beaten Celta Vigo in the Europa League.

Juventus rarely threatened to recover in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard headed Lazio ahead, Gustav Isaksen added a second with an angled finish and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru sealed the result on a late counter-attack. Spalletti said his side had returned from Vigo at 4am on Friday after their 2-1 comeback win, then had time to recover with the performance staff.

He had made six changes, but felt Juventus were slow in both body and thought. His criticism covered the lack of tempo, ideas, running and willingness to work, as well as the team’s weakness in duels and its response when things went wrong. Those concerns followed a previous Juventus defeat that had also prompted scrutiny of the team’s competitive response.

Spalletti was absent from the touchline because of a ban following his altercation with Cagliari’s Fabio Pisacane; assistant Marco Domenichini deputised. Juventus have 11 points after seven league rounds, eight behind the leaders. Football Italia noted that Igor Tudor’s team had one more point at the same stage last season, while Thiago Motta’s side had collected 13.

Supporters who stayed until the final whistle jeered and insulted the squad. Spalletti said the response now had to come on the pitch, rather than the players giving in to events, and identified two areas for review: how he communicates with the team and the working method. He said he needed to examine his relationship with the players and decide what must change.

Speaking to DAZN Italia after the match, Spalletti said Juventus had neither controlled the game nor shown a clear idea of how to shape it. He considered the performance unacceptable and said he would reflect carefully on it. His next task is to determine whether the adjustment lies in his approach to the group, the work itself, or both.

Federica Mancuso has followed Juventus through every high and low she can remember, growing up in Turin where the club was never just a team but a way of life. Her writing focuses on what actually happens on the pitch, breaking down formations, pressing structures, and the tactical decisions that often go unnoticed in match coverage. She believes understanding how Juventus play is just as important as knowing the scoreline.

#1479. Lazio’s Turin win leaves Juventus eight points off Serie A lead

Juventus lost 3-0 at home to Lazio on Sunday, October 18, as goals from Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru kept the visitors level with Inter at the top of Serie A. The result, reported by Football Italia and confirmed in Juventus’ match report, was Lazio’s first league victory in Turin since October 2017.

Lazio took the lead in the 37th minute after a short corner, with Mattia Zaccagni’s delivery finding Provstgaard for a glancing header from close range. Isaksen made it 2-0 in the 66th, controlling Nuno Tavares’ cross-field pass before cutting inside and finding the far bottom corner.

Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, carrying the ball forward from inside his own half before beating Guglielmo Vicario with an angled drive. Juventus had chances to respond: Randal Kolo Muani had an effort ruled out for offside, while Nick Woltemade and Nico Gonzalez both went close. The match statistics showed 58 per cent possession for the hosts and nine shots apiece, but Lazio registered three efforts on target to Juventus’ two.

The loss came after a demanding week. Juventus had beaten Celta Vigo 2-1 away in the Europa League on Thursday, but had managed only one win in their previous four league rounds. Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator and Kamil Grabara were unavailable, while Jeremie Boga returned to the bench. Luciano Spalletti served a touchline ban following his altercation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane, leaving assistant Marco Domenichini in charge from the bench.

Lazio needed the win to remain joint leaders, and the result left the Bianconeri with more ground to make up. According to Corriere della Sera, Juventus sit eighth on 11 points, eight behind Inter and Lazio, who have 19 each. The defeat adds to the concern around a season in which Juventus have struggled to turn performances into league results, following their draw with Cagliari.

Corriere also reports Juventus have a goal difference of +1, compared with +12 for Inter and +10 for Lazio. The standings sharpen the pressure on Juventus to respond in the next league rounds, while Lazio leave Turin with a sizeable result and their place alongside Inter at the summit intact.

He writes with the perspective of someone who genuinely cares about where the club is heading rather than simply reporting what has already happened. His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1478. GdS: Milan score, Ramos struggles – the paradox that Amorim must fix

As the weeks go by Ruben Amorim continues to tweak AC Milan tactically, but a constant theme remains: Goncalo Ramos can’t score consistently.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan are evolving on an almost game-by-game basis, but the only one who remains the same is Ramos. One factor stands out above all: the Portuguese fails to get into the flow of play, not only when the team is struggling but even when they play well and win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His derby stats tragically mirror those reported the previous Wednesday against Bologna: zero shots on target, zero shots off target, zero blocked shots, zero chances created, zero assists. The same story. Even the number of balls played was identical: 31.

Yet they were two very different games. Against Inter, Gonçalo even infuriated Luka Modric, who shortly after the quarter-hour mark unleashed a sharp, angled right-footer that was aimed squarely at Josep Martinez. Ramos was right in the path of the ball, potentially denying a 3-0 goal.

Modric muttered words of frustration under his breath, knowing of course that it was not deliberate sabotage. That incident is proof that there are times when nothing goes right, not even when everyone else is playing with a smile.

Ramos’s first two months resemble Gimenez’s a year ago: just as Santiago couldn’t score but had Massimiliano Allegri’s trust thanks to his backroom work for the team, the same is true for Gonçalo. Unlike Santiago, he has scored three goals, though one was a penalty and one a gift.

In terms of goalscoring, his contribution is completely inadequate compared to expectations, the player’s level, and the club’s investment in bringing him to Milanello. Ramos runs, he battles and he tries to get the team moving forward but he can’t get fully involved.

You can also look at it from the other angle: is it the team that are incapable of giving him service? Perhaps precisely because he’s a striker who roams widely and provides no reference points not only for opposing defenders, but also for his own team-mates.

In any case, he was and remains the starting centre-forward. Partly because Francesco Camarda – in Amorim’s eyes – clearly doesn’t offer enough guarantees, and partly because of Gonçalo’s dirty work, which serves to free up space for others.

It’s no coincidence that Adrien Rabiot is frequently finding the back of the net, and the same goes for Diego Moreira and Alphadjo Cisse, all players who don’t usually hang around in the box.

Furthermore, Milan have recently developed a particular quality: when their shots hit the target, they end up in the back of the net. The two goals against Bologna came with their first two shots, the three against Inter with their first three.

Between the Emilians and the Nerazzurri, Milan have had a total of seven shots on target, squeezing five goals from them: a stratospheric 71%. The million-dollar question, now that Milan are poised for the Scudetto race, is: if Ramos were to unlock himself, how far can this team go?

#1476. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: Lamine Yamal breaks Kylian Mbappe scoring record in Champions League

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 20:21, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 20:33

Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has broken a Kylian Mbappe Champions League record courtesy of his opening goal against Aston Villa.

The 19-year-old phenom unsurprisingly started on the right-hand side of the Blaugrana attack at Camp Nou, and he took just seven minutes to make his mark.

However, Yamal was gifted his historic goal on this occasion, as Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki played a short ball to the under pressure Joao Gomes, who passed straight to Yamal.

The Spain international took the ball under his spell and curled in a fine strike to put La Blaugrana ahead, in turn becoming the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history.

Yamal came into the game level with Mbappe on 13 Champions League goals before turning 20, but the Barcelona phenom has now surpassed his Real Madrid counterpart.

Aston Villa make a mistake at the back and Lamine Yamal makes them pay inside 10 minutes ⚡ ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/1IcWOPMJlt

Yamal has amassed his 14 Champions League goals in 37 games in the competition, in addition to providing as many assists since making his debut in September 2023.

The attacker failed to score in his first season in the tournament, but he found the back of the net five times in the 2024-25 edition as Barcelona progressed to the semi-finals.

Yamal then enjoyed his best scoring season in the Champions League to date in the 2025-26 campaign, netting six times, but he was unable to prevent Barca from exiting in the quarter-finals.

This season, Yamal has already struck three times in Europe's premier tournament, also bagging against Feyenoord and Paris Saint-Germain before breaking Mbappe's record against Villa.

At his current scoring rate, Yamal is averaging 0.38 goals per game in the Champions League, and the 19-year-old could very well continue at the top continental level for more than 15 years.

If the Barcelona prodigy continues finding the net at the same volume in the Champions League, he could end his career with around 80 UCL goals with approximately 210 appearances.

Such a total would currently place Yamal fifth in the Champions League all-time scoring charts, only behind Cristiano Ronaldo (140), Lionel Messi (129), Robert Lewandowski (109) and Karim Benzema (90).

However, Mbappe is currently on 73 goals of his own, and the Real Madrid marksman will almost certainly surpass the 80 mark in due course barring a catastrophe.

#1475. “Where the problems arise” – Vitiello reveals the ‘truth’ that Milan’s derby win exposed

Antonio Vitiello believes that the derby win over Inter offered one very clear lesson regarding AC Milan’s current status.

The mood around Milan has been buoyed by a fourth straight victory against the city rivals, one that was very much needed after the 4-2 loss to Bologna on Wednesday night that featured a second-half collapse.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Three goals in the first half from Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira demonstrated the potential of this team when everyone is healthy. However, the issue has been when Ruben Amorim has not had all his key men out there.

Vitiello published his weekly column for MilanNews and he chose to focus on the major takeaway from the derby, which was the display of the potential of this team, in contrast to the limitations shown a few nights prior against Bologna.

“The tradition continues. AC Milan have dominated recent derbies and confirmed this in their recent 3-1 victory over the Nerazzurri, demonstrating their much better management of the Milanese derby,” he began.

“The atmosphere is galvanised by the victory, and the San Siro match revealed an unquestionable verdict. When Milan field their first team, it’s a completely different story. The Rossoneri with their best players are truly fearsome.

“When Moreira, Rabiot, Modric, Pulisic, Maignan, and company play together, the other teams have to worry. However, this isn’t always possible due to a tight schedule that forces coaches to change line-ups when there are games every three days.

“It’s literally impossible to consistently field the same team, also to avoid injuries. But that’s where the problems arise. In the long run, the teams with deeper squads, those who don’t suffer too many fluctuations when switching from starters to second string players, prevail. And the derby reaffirmed this truth.

“So, to be truly competitive, the team must improve in the next two transfer windows. First in January, with at least a couple of valuable additions, even spending significant sums. And then next summer, with the second batch of strong players. The next moves are already planned.

“Milan will soon announce their new manager, Markus Krosche, who will oversee the transfer market and in January will focus on a central defender, while also evaluating a winger and a striker. Three players to raise the bar after the summer transfer window ended with some shortcomings. An incomplete transfer window to compete on three fronts simultaneously.

“But this time Gerry Cardinale has chosen to take a risk. He said so himself in a recent interview with ClassCNBC. ‘The decision to finish in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League. Looking at how things had gone over the last four years, I realized it was time for a real change,’ said Gerry Cardinale.

“Compared to previous years, when the club prioritized a profitable budget, this time the decision was to finish in the red. The summer expenses, and those expected in the January transfer window, will lead the club to invest in players to strengthen the squad.

“The goal is to return to the Champions League after two years of absence. And there’s no room for error.”

#1474. Jermain Defoe could make dugout comeback four months after abrupt Woking departure - as ex-Premier League star is mooted as potential assistant to Karl Robinson at Bromley

Published: 11:36 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:47 EDT, 3 November 2026

Former Salford City manager Karl Robinson is in the running for the Bromley job and could be joined in the dugout by a Premier League icon.

Daily Mail Sport understands that former Tottenham striker Jermain Defoe, most recently Woking manager, has been discussed as a potential assistant should Robinson be appointed to fill the vacancy left by Andy Woodman, who was dismissed last month.

Defoe left Woking after less than four months following a breakdown in his relationship with the club's director of football.

His departure came in dramatic circumstances, failing to turn up for training on the eve of the new season before calling the club to say he would not be returning.

Robinson previously tried to sign Defoe on a free transfer after he left Scottish club Rangers while Oxford United manager.

Defoe played 496 Premier League games, spread across six clubs, scoring 163 goals.

Jermain Defoe (right) could return to coaching soon as potential assistant manager of Bromley

He is Tottenham's seventh-highest all-time goalscorer and ranks 10th on the Premier League's all-time scoring list.

Having failed to land Defoe as a player, Robinson could yet get his man in management.

Bromley have been assessing several candidates as their managerial search enters its second week.

They have already held talks with Chelsea legend Ashley Cole, who took charge of Serie B club Cesena for three months at the end of last season, while former Oxford United boss Matt Bloomfield is in the frame. Cole was previously assistant manager of England Under-21s.

The Ravens sit bottom of League One and are winless in six matches.

Woodman was sacked after five years in charge, having led Bromley from the National League to League One, with just two wins in ten matches in their maiden season in the third tier.

Speaking on the Inside the 72 podcast this week, Woodman said: 'You have to speak honestly. The easiest way I can sum this up is that when I got the job at Bromley, my first game was Wealdstone and my last game in the league was Leicester.

'I'm pretty disappointed, pretty upset and feel pretty misled in numerous ways and situations.

Defoe could join former Salford City manager Karl Robinson if he takes over at the club

'To give five and a half years of my life to a club and a fan base that I really loved and bought into and gave everything I had and be told in no less than four minutes, thanks, that was it really.

'There's no other way of dressing this up. I'm disappointed but that's football as we know it. Unfortunately, it never surprises me.'

Byron Webster, who made 173 appearances in six years at Bromley, is currently in interim charge at the south-east London club.

Away from footballing matters, former Everton striker and cult hero Victor Anichebe is in the final stages of completing a takeover at Bromley. Anichebe is understood to be involved in the search for a new manager.

These teams are tied on 10 points heading into this contest, with Le Tefece in 12th after losing 2-0 at Marseille the last time out, and Strasbourg a place below them on goal difference thanks to a 5-1 win over Auxerre.

#1471. Juventus host Rennes, beaten on all four European trips to Italy, as Lepaul faces absence

Juventus return to Europa League action against a Rennes side that have lost every European away match they have played in Italy. A third win would strengthen their hold on first place after the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio left them eighth in Serie A.

Juventus need a response, and Europe offers the quickest route to one. Luciano Spalletti’s side host Franck Haise’s Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Matchday 3. They do so as leaders of the league phase. Rennes have four points.

The backdrop is uncomfortable. This is the first match since the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio that left Juventus eighth in Serie A. Spalletti watched that game from the stands while serving a one-match ban. The ban followed a confrontation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane. Assistant Marco Domenichini took charge on the bench.

Afterwards, Spalletti said he needed to take a hard look at his relationship with the players. He also admitted Juventus had been worse than Lazio. The schedule had been tight. The squad got back from Vigo at 4:30am, and it was decided they would not train that day.

The Europa League tells a different story. Juventus opened with a 5-0 home win over N.E.C. Nijmegen on 17 September. A 2-1 win at Celta followed. After that game, the coach spoke of a desire in his side not to settle.

Goals have come freely. Juventus have seven so far. The 2003/04 season is the last time the club hit the eight-goal mark across an opening trio of matches in a major European tournament. Back then, it came in the Champions League.

Randal Kolo Muani is central to that output. He has had a hand in five goals across his last five appearances in the Champions League and Europa League.

A third European win would ease some of the pressure on Spalletti. It would also tighten Juventus’ grip on top spot. The visitors will not make it easy, though. Rennes have lost only once this season.

History favours the hosts. Rennes have lost all four of their European away matches in Italy, each against a different club. Juventus were one of them. In the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final, Juventus won 4-2 on aggregate. Filippo Inzaghi scored both goals in the 2-0 win in Turin. Zinedine Zidane and Alessandro Del Piero were involved in the build-up to the second. The return leg in France ended 2-2.

Rennes’ campaign began with a goalless draw away at Sturm Graz on 16 September. They then beat OFI Crete at home on 15 October.

#1470. Man United break unwanted record against Roma with 17-minute horror show in Champions League

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 20:55

Manchester United have set yet another unwanted club record in their Champions League showdown with Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday evening.

Searching for their first triumph in any competition since thumping Sabah 4-0 in their opening European clash of the season, the Red Devils got off to an all-too familiar disastrous start.

With just 11 minutes gone, Roma caught Man United cold on the right-hand side, where Matias Soule made his way into the box untracked and calmly slotted home past Senne Lammens.

Just six minutes later, Gian Piero Gasperini's men were given the chance to double their lead from the penalty spot, as Ayden Heaven was penalised for a handball from Soule's next attempt.

Donyell Malen calmly sent Lammens the wrong way, thus providing Roma with a comfortable cushion and writing another dismal chapter of history for Man Utd in the process.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box ? https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES

Having conceded twice inside just 17 minutes, Man United set a new record for the earliest time they have fallen 2-0 down in a home game in a major European competition.

Red Devils fans had already been protesting against the Glazers and INEOS before the game, and disgruntled supporters soon made their frustrations known in a disruptive manner.

Some members of the Old Trafford crowd threw tennis balls onto the pitch behind the Roma goal, and attacker Matheus Cunha took it upon himself to remove them.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada are both present at the Theatre of Dreams for the clash with Roma, while anti-Jim Ratcliffe and Glazers chants could also be heard.

The half-time whistle unsurprisingly triggered a cacophony of boos from the home crowd, while Alan Shearer described the Red Devils' performance as "absolutely atrocious" on Amazon Prime.

Man Utd fans are not happy. https://t.co/7yc9jwqz7u

Barring possession, the half-time statistics told the story of a Man United side who were thoroughly dominated by their Italian counterparts, who were full value for their two-goal advantage.

Michael Carrick's men generated a paltry 0.24 Expected Goals to Roma's 1.48, and they could count themselves lucky that their visitors were not further in the ascendancy at the break.

Shortly before the whistle blew, Soule curled a fizzing left-footed strike just wide of the post, as Gasperini's men continuously carved out opportunities against a disjointed Man Utd defence.

Defeat for the Red Devils would mark fourth third in a row across all competitions, and also extend their winless run to 10 matches, although Carrick is expected to remain in charge until the international break regardless of tonight's result.

#1469. Sky Germany: Krösche heading for Milan but compensation must be discussed – the situation

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Now, Sky Germany confirm that Krösche’s future likely lies in Italy because a move to Milan is becoming increasingly likely. However, no deal has been finalised yet: officials from both clubs still need to hold talks as Krösche is only on leave from Frankfurt.

His contract, which runs until 2028, is currently still valid. The 46-year-old insisted on having a release clause included in his contract. Specifically, this means that any club wanting to hire him before the summer of 2027 will have to pay a fee of approximately €5-7m, or negotiate with Eintracht.

No advanced talks have yet taken place, but Sky do add that Krösche is expected to take on the role of Head of Football with Milan. A start date of January 1, 2027 – coinciding with the start of the winter transfer window – is being discussed.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

Paris Saint-Germain broke an outrageous Champions League goalscoring record in their first-half rout of Villarreal on Tuesday evening.

Luis Enrique's men travelled to La Ceramica aiming to make it four wins from four in the 2026-27 tournament after getting the better of Slovan Bratislava, Manchester City and Barcelona in the opening three rounds.

Les Parisiens got off to the best start imaginable against their La Liga counterparts, as Joao Neves broke the deadlock inside nine minutes before Desire Doue doubled the lead in the 12th.

Senny Mayulu added a third for PSG less than a minute after Villarreal had kicked off again, before Fabian Ruiz got in on the act with the visitors' fourth just a few moments later.

After successfully completing their quest for back-to-back Champions League titles in 2025-26, PSG seemed to have lost their golden touch at the start of the current campaign.

#1464. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

#1463. Bayer Leverkusen vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 03 Nov 2026 21:33

Bayer Leverkusen's perfect Europa League record comes under threat again when Marseille travel to face them at BayArena on Thursday.

The hosts boast three wins from three in Europe so far, and their tally of nine points means they are second in the league-phase table, whereas visitors Marseille are third last in 34th place with no points.

Leverkusen's previous match in the Europa League was a 2-0 victory against OFI Crete on October 22, and they have now scored eight goals and kept three clean sheets in the tournament.

Carles Martinez's side have since played three games in all competitions, losing twice in the Bundesliga while beating Nurnberg 5-2 in the DFB-Pokal on October 28.

Their latest result was a 4-2 league defeat against Stuttgart on Saturday, and that loss left them sixth in the top flight with 13 points after eight matchweeks.

Die Werkself's clash with Stuttgart ended their perfect record at home, with the club having won their first five games at BayArena in 2026-27.

Marseille's campaign has been far from straightforward, though they have at least started to find form in Ligue 1 given they have won their past four fixtures in the division.

The French side are sixth in the table with 15 points from a possible 27, but only three points separate them from second-placed Lille and five points from first-placed Paris Saint-Germain.

While head coach Bruno Genesio came under immense pressure at the start of the season following an opening stretch of five losses and one triumph, he has since overseen four wins from six games.

Les Olympiens scored 13 goals in those six matches, though they conceded on seven occasions and kept just two clean sheets.

Marseille's form on their travels has been poor for some time considering they have been beaten in seven of their past 10 away contests, and they have lost four of their six away clashes this season.

Bayer Leverkusen form (all competitions):

Bayer Leverkusen are dealing with an injury crisis in attack, with forwards Eliesse Ben Seghir, Martin Terrier, Christian Kofane and Moussa Diaby all ruled out.

The hosts may have no other option but to field Lucas Vazquez, Ibrahim Maza and Afonso Moreira behind striker Patrik Schick.

With right-back Guela Doue still set for a few weeks on the treatment table, former Liverpool defender Jarell Quansah is the obvious option on the right.

As for Marseille, left-back Emerson Palmieri avoided a serious injury against Toulouse on Sunday, but perhaps Ulisses Garcia will be used on Thursday.

Midfielders Tochukwu Nnadi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and Himad Abdelli are set to play together, and they will be expected to support striker Amine Gouiri.

Bayer Leverkusen possible starting lineup:

Flekken; Quansah, Medina, Tapsoba, Gutierrez; Fernandez, Garcia; Vazquez, Maza, Moreira; Schick

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Nnadi, Hojbjerg, Abdelli; Harit, Gouiri, Paixao

Leverkusen may have struggled for consistency in domestic football, but they have been excellent in Europe so far.

Despite their injury woes, the hosts should still believe they can beat Marseille, who have rarely travelled well in recent months.

#1462. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.
